#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Lazy DRAFT create for the release train's asset-upload steps (gh-1801).
#
# The train workflows (ci.yml binaries/web-spa, build-macos.yml
# build-macos-cli/build-extension) need a release object to attach assets
# to, but the release must never go live from an upload step: `fa update`
# resolves the `latest` release and hard-fails without the SIGNED
# SHA256SUMS(.sig) (bin/self_manage.dart provenance gate), which only the
# tag-run release-provenance job can upload. This script creates the
# release as a DRAFT — nothing else:
#
#   - body = scripts/release_notes.sh output (curated `## <version>`
#     CHANGELOG section → curated `## Unreleased` → conventional commits;
#     the gh-1172 curated-notes contract), with a minimal fallback —
#     never `--generate-notes` (review threads 3/7);
#   - body carries `<!-- release-draft-owner: run/<run_id>/job/<job> -->`
#     so scripts/release_draft_guard.sh can reclaim the draft on failure
#     (review threads 4/8) — matrix legs override the identity via
#     RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY (e.g. binaries-linux-x64) so a failed leg's
#     guard can never match a sibling's in-flight draft;
#   - the view→create race is tolerated (`|| true`): a sibling leg or the
#     attach path may create the release between our view and create —
#     the loser just uploads into the winner's release;
#   - it NEVER publishes and NEVER flags latest: the single publish point
#     of a tag train is release-provenance's "Upload provenance assets"
#     step (`gh release edit --draft=false --latest` after SHA256SUMS.sig
#     lands). A red provenance leaves the previous release as latest —
#     safe degradation, never a provenance-less latest (v1.0.630 window).
#
# Usage: release_lazy_draft.sh <tag>
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GITHUB_RUN_ID, GITHUB_JOB (Actions defaults),
#      RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY (optional leg-suffixed override),
#      GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN.
set -euo pipefail

tag="${1:?usage: release_lazy_draft.sh <tag>}"
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
identity="${RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY:-run/${GITHUB_RUN_ID:?GITHUB_RUN_ID must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}/job/${GITHUB_JOB:?GITHUB_JOB must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}}"

# The guard greps exactly this class — validate here so a malformed
# override fails loud instead of stamping a marker the guard could never
# match (a forever-orphaned draft).
printf '%s' "$identity" | grep -Eq '^run/[0-9]+/job/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$' || {
  echo "::error::RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY '$identity' does not match 'run/<id>/job/<name>' — the draft lifecycle guard could never reclaim such a draft" >&2
  exit 1
}

# Already created (by a sibling leg, the attach path, or a previous run)?
# Drafts and published releases both resolve here — upload-only is safe.
if gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "release $tag already exists — lazy draft create skipped"
  exit 0
fi

# Body: curated notes (CHANGELOG section / Unreleased / conventional
# commits) plus the ownership marker the guard verifies before deleting.
# stderr is NOT swallowed: release_notes.sh's ::error gates (e.g. the
# duplicate-'## Unreleased' curation guard) must stay visible even when
# the minimal fallback below keeps the train moving.
notes_file="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/release-lazy-notes.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -f "$notes_file"' EXIT
if ! bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_notes.sh" "$tag" >"$notes_file" ||
  [ ! -s "$notes_file" ]; then
  printf 'Release %s — see the CHANGELOG.\n' "$tag" >"$notes_file"
fi
marker="<!-- release-draft-owner: $identity -->"
grep -qF "$marker" "$notes_file" || printf '\n%s\n' "$marker" >>"$notes_file"

# DRAFT-first (gh-1801): a create here must never publish — the resolved
# asset list at this point can never include the signed checksums. The
# race-lost create is tolerated (the winner owns the release).
gh release create "$tag" \
  --repo "$repo" \
  --title "$tag" \
  --draft \
  --notes-file "$notes_file" || true
echo "✅ lazy draft ready for $tag (owner $identity) — publish is provenance-owned (gh-1801)"

- feat(gh-1844): media slots never fall back to the main connection
  implicitly — SDK/CLI, app store, and the JS bridge resolve a slot
  without an override as UNCONFIGURED with an actionable
  "configure the slot" error; the main connection serves a slot only via
  the explicit per-slot `useMainConnection: true` opt-in (YAML
  `models.slots.<slot>.useMainConnection` / app's "Same as main
  connection" pick, preserved through `media_models.json`). Image and
  video generation accept multimodal input (text + reference images:
  sandbox paths, http(s) URLs, base64) on capability-declaring
  OpenRouter endpoints (`input_references` + declared/probed
  `input_modalities` gate; unsupported endpoints fail before any network
  call); the OpenRouter video job API is a first-class video dialect
  (submit → poll → mp4). New `decide` tool: structured decisions via
  OpenRouter's Decisions API (`/v1/systemone`) — bool/choice/score
  questions with calibrated probabilities, structured error results, no
  streaming.

- feat(gh-1834): the FinalizeGate contract counts a parity/conformance
  claim as verified only with negative + combination self-checks — new
  numbered step 2.6 in `prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md` (refused
  incompatible/mutually exclusive options, empty/corrupt inputs, boundary
  values, must-NOT-work cases, alongside happy paths; a blanket
  "everything matches" is not verified). Universality: abstract example
  only, no benchmark/task/flag names in the prompt; the step is
  conditional, so tasks with no conformance claim see no gate change.
  Ledger/verdict wire formats unchanged; validated end-to-end by the
  scripted IT-4 replay (real CLI + real bash) whose persisted
  `task_ledger` carries the rejection rows.

- fix(gh-1832): release v1.0.635 published without `fa-extension.zip` — the
  landing-page download 404'd. The extension's only producer (the daily
  `build-macos.yml` build-extension leg) derives its tag as "latest+1 at its
  own dispatch moment"; on 2026-10-24 the `v1.0.635` tag was cut by
  `auto_release` before those legs ran, so the extension (and the DMGs)
  landed on an orphaned `v1.0.636` draft while the tag train published
  v1.0.635 — every leg green, nothing asserted the published asset set.
  Now `scripts/release_required_assets.txt` is the single source of truth,
  `scripts/assert_release_assets.sh` gates the `release-provenance` publish
  flip (a missing asset leaves the release a draft and fails the run
  loudly) and a new `release-asset-smoke` ci.yml job post-publish probes
  every landing-page release link + the full required set (red on non-200).
  Remediation: the exact-tag `fa-extension.zip` (built from the v1.0.635
  tree by run 40064876732) was uploaded to release v1.0.635 — the landing
  link serves 200 again.

- fix(gh-1820): the arm64 DMG leg's stale size floor is reseeded onto the
  shipped v1.0.634 shape — run 4004758753 (post-#1815 SPM-lane adoption)
  passed the min-platform gate and the full build, then failed the
  `size_manifest.py` +5% budget on `App.framework/App` +5.1%
  (25,020,112 → 26,284,144, the accumulated Dart AOT of #1793/#1794/

  `test/ci_1820_macos_arm64_size_floor_test.dart` gates the shape green
  through the REAL `size_manifest.py check` and pins the committed floor
  byte-identical to a `--reseed` round-trip.

- fix(gh-1814): the desktop DMG lane ADOPTS the SwiftPM lane — Flutter
  3.47.7 removed the FLUTTER_SWIFT_PACKAGE_MANAGER disable knob
  (flutter/flutter#193978), so the gh-180 pure-CocoaPods pin became a no-op
  and the min-platform gate (which forbade any SwiftPM state) failed both
  DMG legs on every pinned-3.47.7 run (39991663029, 40022900373); the
  #1813 escape (pin 3.47.4) is unreachable on the ~60kB/s runner link.
  `scripts/assert_macos_min_platform.sh` now ASSERTS the SPM lane instead:
  SwiftPM state expected after `flutter build macos --config-only`,
  generated package floor ≥ the app floor (the silent bump must not skip —
  the original gh-180 killer), no SwiftPM product above the app minimum,

  composer while the slash menu is open — the vendored dart_tui decoder

  longer signal its own shell or the harness. Scripts are delivered from a
  per-exec private temp file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>`) so the wrapper
  argv never carries the script body (`pkill -f <pattern>` cannot
  self-match its own `sh -c`; `$0`/`$#`/exit codes/`set -e`/stdin stay

  POSIX installer copied the bundle libs beside the binary
  (`<install_dir>/lib`), so `read path=x.db` died with a raw FFI dump
  (`Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load
  dynamic library '~/.local/lib/libsqlite3.dylib'`); it only worked on machines
  with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. Fixed the layout in all three

  migrate. The POSIX installers also report a failed lib copy instead of
  swallowing it (`site/install.sh` warns naming the lib dir; same in
  `install_local.sh`), and `site/install.sh.template` carries the same
  layout so regenerating the installers cannot resurrect the old one.

release-provenance:
    name: Sign release checksums
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [binaries, web-spa, build-extension]
    timeout-minutes: 10
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.binaries.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: write # upload SHA256SUMS(.sig) to the GitHub Release
    steps:
      # gh-814 r2: the trust-anchor drift gate below diffs the secret's public
      # key against the PEM embedded in site/install.sh — that file must be
      # present, so the signing job checks out the site/ tree.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Collect release assets
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p provenance
          gh release download "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" \
            --dir provenance --pattern 'fa-*'
          ls -l provenance

      # gh-1832: PUBLISH-BLOCKING required-assets gate. The single source of
      # truth is scripts/release_required_assets.txt, consumed by
      # scripts/assert_release_assets.sh. v1.0.635 published without
      # fa-extension.zip because the extension's only producer (the daily
      # build-macos.yml build-extension leg) attached it to a "latest+1"
      # draft while this train published the tagged release — every leg
      # green, nothing asserted the published set. A missing asset here
      # fails the release run loudly and leaves the release a DRAFT (the
      # previous release stays latest) instead of publishing a partial one.
      - name: Assert required release assets (gh-1832 gate)
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: bash scripts/assert_release_assets.sh "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"

      - name: Build and sign SHA256SUMS
        env:
          FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY }}
        run: |
          cd provenance
          sha256sum fa-* > SHA256SUMS
          if [ -z "$FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY" ]; then
            echo "::error::FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY is not set — refusing to publish a release without signed checksums (SEC-07 #795, fail-closed). Set the repo secret with the release-signing private key."
            exit 1
          fi
          printf '%s' "$FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          chmod 600 "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          # The key never outlives the step — trap covers mid-step failure.
          trap 'rm -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"' EXIT
          openssl dgst -sha256 -sign "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key" -out SHA256SUMS.sig SHA256SUMS
          # Self-check: the signature must verify against OUR OWN public key
          # before anything is uploaded.
          openssl rsa -in "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key" -pubout -out pub.pem 2>/dev/null
          openssl dgst -sha256 -verify pub.pem -signature SHA256SUMS.sig SHA256SUMS
          rm -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          # gh-814 r2 trust-anchor drift gate (fail-closed): the public key
          # derived from the secret must equal the PEM embedded in
          # site/install.sh — otherwise every pinned installer would ship an
          # anchor that rejects this release's signed checksums.
          sed -n '/BEGIN PUBLIC KEY/,/END PUBLIC KEY/p' "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/site/install.sh" |
            sed "1s/^.*BEGIN/-----BEGIN/; \$s/END.*\$/END PUBLIC KEY-----/" > embedded-anchor.pem
          openssl pkey -pubin -in embedded-anchor.pem -noout ||
            { echo "::error::site/install.sh trust anchor does not parse as a public key — regenerate installers (dart run scripts/gen_installers.dart)"; exit 1; }
          cmp embedded-anchor.pem pub.pem ||
            { echo "::error::FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY drifted from the trust anchor embedded in site/install.sh — rotate the keypair: update install.signing_public_key in site/install-config.yaml, regenerate installers, and update the repo secret TOGETHER. Refusing to sign (fail-closed)."; exit 1; }
          rm -f pub.pem embedded-anchor.pem

      - name: Upload provenance assets
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          gh release upload "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" \
            provenance/SHA256SUMS provenance/SHA256SUMS.sig \
            --clobber --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
          # gh-1801 (rework): THE publish point of the train. The release
          # now carries every fa-* asset AND the signed SHA256SUMS(.sig) —
          # the first moment `fa update` can actually serve it (it
          # hard-fails without the signed checksums, bin/self_manage.dart).
          # Flip draft=false + latest here and ONLY here: a red provenance
          # leaves the previous release as latest (safe degradation)
          # instead of stranding a provenance-less one (the v1.0.630
          # empty/partial-latest window class).
          gh release edit "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --draft=false --latest --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"

  # gh-1832 AC3: post-publish smoke. Probes (1) EVERY releases/(latest/)?
  # download/ URL the fa1.dev landing page exposes (site/index.html) and
  # (2) the full required set from scripts/release_required_assets.txt via
  # a 1-byte ranged GET each — red on anything but HTTP 200/206. Rides the
  # tag train only (PR runs never probe release URLs); a 404 here is the
  # owner-facing v1.0.635 symptom caught the same hour it appears.
  release-asset-smoke:
    name: Release asset smoke (landing links + required set)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: release-provenance
    timeout-minutes: 10
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.release-provenance.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Probe every landing-page release link
        run: bash scripts/assert_release_assets.sh --landing site/index.html
      - name: Probe the full required asset set
        env:
          GITHUB_REPOSITORY: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: bash scripts/assert_release_assets.sh --smoke "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"

  # Advance the vpinned release marker to the freshly signed tag. PURE
  # RELEASE-ARTIFACT MANIPULATION — no commits, no pushes: pin_release.sh
  # re-verifies the target's signature itself (fail-closed), then uploads
  # the PINNED_VERSION asset to the standing `vpinned` release. Runs after
  # release-provenance so the signed SHA256SUMS it checks are already
  # published. The marker is only a pointer — installers verify the pointed
  # release's signature against the committed trust anchor, so a tampered
  # marker degrades to a DoS, never a bad binary.
  install-pin-bump:
    name: Advance vpinned marker
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: release-provenance
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # always(): when release-provenance FAILS (e.g. the binaries/signature
    # upload race), plain needs-gating leaves this job SKIPPED — and a
    # `rerun --failed` never resurrects skipped jobs, so the marker stays
    # stale forever (v1.0.483: publish+provenance flaked, the recovery rerun
    # went green, the marker never advanced). With always() the job RUNS
    # even after a failed provenance: pin_release.sh's own pre-move
    # provenance gate (check_install_pin.sh with FA_PIN_TARGET) fails the
    # job loudly instead of moving the marker — and a FAILED job IS part of
    # rerun --failed, so the recovery cascade reaches it.
    if: >-
      always() && github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Point the vpinned marker at ${{ github.ref_name }}
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: bash scripts/pin_release.sh "${{ github.ref_name }}"

  installer-smoke:
    name: Installer smoke
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    needs: [binaries, release-provenance]
    timeout-minutes: 15
    # Depends on binaries — no !cancelled() needed here: the skip chain is
    # already broken upstream by the binaries job's own guard (fa#456).
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - os: windows-latest
            kind: ps1
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            kind: sh
          - os: macos-latest
            kind: sh
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Run the one-line installer (PowerShell)
        if: matrix.kind == 'ps1'
        shell: pwsh
        run: ./site/install.ps1

      - name: Run the one-line installer (sh)
        if: matrix.kind == 'sh'
        shell: bash
        env:
          FA_INSTALL_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/fa-bin
        run: sh ./site/install.sh

      - name: Smoke the installed binary (Windows)
        if: matrix.kind == 'ps1'
        shell: pwsh
        run: '& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Fa\bin\fa.exe" --version'

      - name: Smoke the installed binary (Unix)

if: always()
        run: |
          security delete-keychain build-${{ matrix.arch }}.keychain 2>/dev/null || true
          rm -f certificate.p12 installer.p12

  build-macos-cli:
    name: Build macOS CLI ${{ matrix.arch }}
    needs: version
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    # Ceiling for the daily cli watcher's budget arithmetic (#351): dart
    # CLI bundle + release upload; the two arches run in PARALLEL on
    # GitHub-hosted runners (they do not serialize like the self-hosted
    # build-macos matrix does).
    timeout-minutes: 45
    if: inputs.create_release == 'true'
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - runner: macos-latest
            arch: arm64
          - runner: macos-15-intel
            arch: x64
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # Blobless full history: the lazy draft create (gh-1801 rework)
          # builds the release body via scripts/release_notes.sh — same
          # reason as release-macos's checkout (gh-1477: the notes read
          # commit MESSAGES, never historical file blobs).
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Build CLI bundle
        run: |
          version="${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}"
          dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=build/out
          mv build/out/bundle/bin/fah build/out/bundle/bin/fa
          chmod +x build/out/bundle/bin/fa
          echo "$version" > build/out/bundle/version.txt

      - name: Ad-hoc sign CLI binary
        run: |
          codesign --force --sign - build/out/bundle/bin/fa

      - name: Archive and upload CLI bundle
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
          # Matrix legs share GITHUB_JOB=build-macos-cli — the leg-suffixed
          # draft owner identity keeps the guard below scoped to the leg
          # that created the draft, never the sibling's mid-upload one.
          RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY: run/${{ github.run_id }}/job/${{ github.job }}-${{ matrix.arch }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          asset="fa-macos-${{ matrix.arch }}.tar.gz"
          tar -czf "$asset" -C build/out bundle
          ls -lh "$asset"

          # gh-1801 (rework): DRAFT-first, publish is PROVENANCE-OWNED.
          # The CLI tarball is a `fa update` asset, but servability needs
          # the SIGNED SHA256SUMS — which only the tag-run's
          # release-provenance job uploads (ci.yml). So: create the draft
          # lazily (curated notes via release_notes.sh + THIS leg's
          # draft-owner marker the guard below can reclaim), upload, and
          # let provenance own the --draft=false --latest flip.
          bash scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh "$RELEASE_TAG"
          gh release upload "$RELEASE_TAG" "$asset" --clobber --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"

      # Draft lifecycle invariant (issue #282): this job creates releases,
      # so a failed/cancelled run must not leave one behind as a draft.
      # Leg-scoped (gh-1801): matches only THIS arch leg's marker.
      - name: Draft lifecycle guard (delete orphaned draft on failure)
        if: always() && job.status != 'success'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
          RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY: run/${{ github.run_id }}/job/${{ github.job }}-${{ matrix.arch }}
        run: bash scripts/release_draft_guard.sh "$RELEASE_TAG"

  build-extension:
    name: Build Chrome extension
    needs: version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily cli watcher's budget arithmetic (#351).
    timeout-minutes: 30
    if: inputs.create_release == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # Blobless full history: the lazy draft create (gh-1801 rework)
          # builds the release body via scripts/release_notes.sh — same
          # reason as release-macos's checkout (gh-1477).
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          # gh-1684 decision 4 (gate symmetry): the SAME exact patch pin
          # the pages.yml leg carried and the PR gate carries (#1431 —
          # the rev normalization absorbs canvaskit rev-hash churn, the
          # pin keeps every fa-extension.zip build comparable across
          # legs). The old unpinned `channel: stable` floated the engine
          # per run — one of the two ways the release and Pages legs
          # diverged.
          flutter-version: '3.47.7'
          channel: stable

      - name: dart pub get (root)
        run: dart pub get

      # browser_ext/dart is a separate package (path dep on this root), so
      # its pub get must follow the root's — same as browser-ext.yml.
      - name: dart pub get (browser_ext/dart)
        run: cd browser_ext/dart && dart pub get

      # Full artifact: SW agent (dart2js) + the Flutter panel app embedded,
      # exactly what "Load unpacked" expects. --clobber keeps the stable
      # asset name fa-extension.zip pointing at the newest build (the
      # landing page links it directly).
      - name: Build extension zip
        run: bash scripts/build_browser_ext.sh --with-app

      # AC1 (#1096): per-entry uncompressed size table + +5% budget gate
      # against the committed baseline (gh-1684: reseeded to the
      # post-#1631 vendored-engines shape — litert/transformers/webllm are
      # intentional CWS policy; growth beyond the floor fails the release).
      # Identical invocation as the PR-time gate (ci.yml
      # extension-size-gate): one baseline, one enforcement rule.
      - name: Size manifest + budget gate (fa-extension.zip)
        run: python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check build/fa-extension.zip --baseline scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv

      - name: Upload extension to the release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          asset="fa-extension.zip"
          cp build/fa-extension.zip "$asset"
          ls -lh "$asset"

          # extension zip is not a `fa update` asset — and even a CLI
          # asset alone would not make the release servable: the SIGNED
          # SHA256SUMS only lands in the tag-run's release-provenance job,
          # which owns the --draft=false --latest flip. Create the draft
          # with the curated notes + the draft-owner marker (so the guard
          # step below can reclaim it on failure) and upload.
          bash scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh "$RELEASE_TAG"
          gh release upload "$RELEASE_TAG" "$asset" --clobber --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"

      # Draft lifecycle invariant (issue #282): this job creates releases,
      # so a failed/cancelled run must not leave one behind as a draft.
      - name: Draft lifecycle guard (delete orphaned draft on failure)
        if: always() && job.status != 'success'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
        run: bash scripts/release_draft_guard.sh "$RELEASE_TAG"

  release-macos:
    name: Create macOS GitHub Release
    needs: [version, build-macos]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily cli watcher's budget arithmetic (#351).
    timeout-minutes: 15
    if: inputs.create_release == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # Full history: release_notes.sh falls back to "commits since the
          # previous tag" when the CHANGELOG has no section for this version.
          # gh-1477: blobless — the notes read commit MESSAGES, never
          # historical file blobs.
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - name: Download DMG artifacts
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          path: dmgs
          pattern: Fa-macos-*
          merge-multiple: true

      - name: List downloaded artifacts
        run: ls -laR dmgs/

      - name: Merge macOS auto-update manifest
        run: |
          python3 -m pip install --user pyyaml
          chmod +x scripts/merge-mac-update-manifest.sh
          scripts/merge-mac-update-manifest.sh dmgs dmgs/latest-mac.yml
          cat dmgs/latest-mac.yml

      - name: Create or update GitHub Release
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          # PAT (not the job token) so the tag push fires tag CI — the
          # attach-or-create script builds its push URL only when GH_TOKEN
          # is set; without it `git push ""` died with "fatal: bad
          # repository ''" (2026-10-22 v1.0.626 mobile leg).
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
          VERSION: ${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          DMGS=$(ls dmgs/*.dmg 2>/dev/null || true)
          ZIPS=$(ls dmgs/*-mac.zip 2>/dev/null || true)
          MANIFEST="dmgs/latest-mac.yml"
          echo "DMGs to upload: $DMGS"
          echo "ZIPs to upload: $ZIPS"

          STABLE_COPIES=()
          for zip in $ZIPS; do
            base=$(basename "$zip")
            # Skip no-sandbox zips from the auto-update stable names; the
            # sandboxed build is the default update feed.
            if [[ "$base" == *nosandbox* ]]; then
              continue
            fi
            if [[ "$base" == *arm64* ]]; then
              cp "$zip" "dmgs/fa-macos-arm64-mac.zip"
              STABLE_COPIES+=("dmgs/fa-macos-arm64-mac.zip")
            elif [[ "$base" == *x86_64* ]]; then
              cp "$zip" "dmgs/fa-macos-x64-mac.zip"
              STABLE_COPIES+=("dmgs/fa-macos-x64-mac.zip")
            fi
          done

          # Extract the raw binary from the .app bundle and upload it as the
          # plain asset name (fa-macos-arm64 / fa-macos-x64) so `fa update`
          # and direct downloads work without knowing the version suffix.
          for zip in $ZIPS; do
            base=$(basename "$zip")
            if [[ "$base" == *nosandbox* ]]; then
              continue
            fi
            unzip -qo "$zip" -d /tmp/fa-extract >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
            BIN="/tmp/fa-extract/Fa.app/Contents/MacOS/Fa"
            if [ -f "$BIN" ]; then
              if [[ "$base" == *arm64* ]]; then
                cp "$BIN" "dmgs/fa-macos-arm64"
                ASSETS+=("dmgs/fa-macos-arm64")
              elif [[ "$base" == *x86_64* ]]; then
                cp "$BIN" "dmgs/fa-macos-x64"
                ASSETS+=("dmgs/fa-macos-x64")
              fi
              chmod +x "dmgs/fa-macos-arm64" "dmgs/fa-macos-x64" 2>/dev/null || true
            fi
            rm -rf /tmp/fa-extract
          done
          ASSETS=($DMGS $ZIPS $MANIFEST "${STABLE_COPIES[@]}")

          # Notes come from the CHANGELOG section for this version, with a
          # conventional-commit fallback (issue #282: no more filler
          # bodies); the install hints stay as a footer.
          bash scripts/release_notes.sh "$RELEASE_TAG" > release-notes.md || true
          printf '\n## Installation\n- **macOS**: Download the DMG for your architecture (`arm64` for Apple Silicon, `x86_64` for Intel) and drag Fa.app to Applications. In-app updates use the ZIP + latest-mac.yml feed.\n- **Linux**: Download tar.gz, extract and run the `bundle/fa` binary.\n- **Windows**: Download zip, extract and run the `fa.exe`.\n' >> release-notes.md

          # Attach-or-create (issue #282 E3 + review of #294): idempotent
          # against the view->create race - a lost race uploads into the
          # winner's release instead of failing - and the create stamps an
          # ownership marker into the draft body, so the guard step below
          # only ever deletes THIS job's draft, never the mobile leg's
          # mid-upload draft on the same derived tag.
          bash scripts/release_attach_or_create.sh "$RELEASE_TAG" "${ASSETS[@]}"

      # Draft lifecycle invariant (issue #282): the create above uploads
      # assets through a draft — a failed/cancelled run must delete it,
      # never orphan it (the v0.1.190 rot). Ownership-scoped (review of
      # #294): the guard deletes only a draft whose body carries THIS
      # run+job's marker — a sibling leg's draft is never touched.
      - name: Draft lifecycle guard (delete orphaned draft on failure)
        if: always() && job.status != 'success'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
        run: bash scripts/release_draft_guard.sh "$RELEASE_TAG"

The draft v1.0.642 remained orphaned (owner run failed but the guard only fires on the job's own failure).

Then: v1.0.642 tag was pushed at 09:00:29 (release created 09:00:29 by IstiN... the auto-release or the tag train attached to the EXISTING draft). Release v1.0.642 published 10:29:16 — so the tag train found the existing draft and provenance published it. Draft created 09:00:29, published 10:29:16. OK so v1.0.642 ended fine.

Now — the sweep saw stale drafts v1.0.637, v1.0.639, v1.0.641 on 10-26 05:29. Let me now check: the previous daily sweep issues — was there an issue about 637/639 earlier? Actually the important thing: WHY was v1.0.641 a DRAFT at sweep time when the tag train published it at 05:11:35 on 10-25?

Look at the timeline again:
- 10-25 04:50:47: tag v1.0.641 pushed → ci run 40163369302 → draft created.
- 10-25 05:11:35: provenance published v1.0.641 (draft=false, latest).
- 10-25 05:25: daily leg run 40165498619 starts, derives v1.0.642, creates draft v1.0.642.
- v1.0.642 train publishes at 10:29:16. Wait — but for the v1.0.642 train to publish, provenance ran on tag v1.0.642 at 09:00. Fine.
- 10-26 05:17: daily-publish run 40274465122 → sweep at 05:29 finds v1.0.641 as a DRAFT?!

Hmm — wait. Maybe there's a LATER build-macos daily run on 10-26? Run 40274586545 created 10-26T05:30:28 (after the sweep). What about between 10-25 10:29 and 10-26 05:29? The list shows build-macos runs: 40274586545 (10-26 05:30), 40165498619 (10-25 05:25). Nothing between.

Hmm, what about build-mobile daily leg runs? The play leg was green... build-mobile runs on 10-25/26? The play leg dispatches build-mobile.yml with android_content=all — that derives its own tag latest+1 and attaches ABs. Let me check build-mobile runs. release_attach_or_create.sh in build-mobile release-mobile job (line 1517). If a build-mobile daily run at ~05:2x on 10-25 derived tag... latest at that moment = v1.0.641 (published 05:11). latest+1 = v1.0.642. It would attach ABs to v1.0.642 draft. Fine.

OK here's another thought — maybe the sweep didn't see v1.0.641 draft at all; maybe the ISSUE BODY is accurate but there's a subtlety: could v1.0.641 have been RE-DRAFTED by `gh release edit`? Nobody does that...

WAIT. Actually — `gh release create` with an EXISTING tag... In release_attach_or_create.sh, if `gh release view` fails (release missing) but the TAG exists, it creates a draft with assets. If the release EXISTS (published v1.0.641), it uploads + since SHA256SUMS present → `gh release edit --draft=false --latest`. Fine.

Hmm, but what about the mobile leg's release_attach_or_create racing... no.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Auto-release (gh-1522): cut the annotated TAG + GitHub Release directly —
# the git tag is the single source of truth for versions and ZERO files are
# mutated in-repo. The retired flow (this script used to patch-bump
# pubspec.yaml / CHANGELOG.md / flutter_app/pubspec.{yaml,lock} and push a
# 'chore(release):' commit straight to protected main) landed a 4-file bot
# commit on main per release: noisy history, a direct-to-main bot push
# path, CHANGELOG growth toward the pub.dev 256 KiB cap (gh-1452), and
# pubspec.lock churn that invalidated flutter_app's --enforce-lockfile
# (gh-1265). Now:
#
#   latest tag + 1  →  `git tag -a v$next origin/main`  →  push the tag
#
# NO GitHub Release is created here (gh-1801): this script has an EMPTY
# resolved asset list, and creating the release would publish an empty
# `latest` that breaks `fa update` until the binaries backfill. The
# tag-run binaries job owns release creation — draft-first, published
# only after an asset upload lands.
#
# Runs in CI on every push to main / the 2h catch-up cron / manual dispatch
# (the `release` job in .github/workflows/ci.yml). The job authenticates via
# actions/create-github-app-token (RELEASE_APP_ID + RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY);
# the App token pushes the tag because GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger the
# tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs (gh-1172). The App remains the ONLY
# bypass actor on the main ruleset but no longer needs to push to main at
# all — releases never touch the branch.
#
# The tag push fires the ci.yml `publish` job, which stamps the staged
# publish tree from the SAME tag (scripts/stage_publish_package.sh <dir>
# <version>) — the tag↔staged-version invariant is guarded there.
#
# Dry-run: RELEASE_DRY_RUN=1 (or "true") computes the tag that WOULD be
# cut, logs it, and stops before any push.
#
# Release notes: scripts/release_notes.sh is NOT invoked here anymore —
# with no release create there is no body to prepare. The release body is
# owned by the tag-run binaries job's lazy draft create
# (scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh), which folds the curated CHANGELOG
# section via release_notes.sh into the DRAFT it creates; the signed
# provenance job publishes it (gh-1801).
set -euo pipefail

# Tag authorship names the App so releases are attributable in history
# (auditability contract, gh-1172).
git config user.name "fa-release-bot[bot]"
git config user.email "fa-release-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"

dry_run=0
case "${RELEASE_DRY_RUN:-0}" in 1|true|yes) dry_run=1 ;; esac

# Coalescing guards: pub.dev rate-limits publishes (~12/day), so releases are
# capped at one per 2h; runs with nothing new since the last tag are skipped.
git fetch origin main --tags --quiet
last_tag=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || true)
if [ -n "$last_tag" ]; then
  pending=$(git rev-list --count "$last_tag..origin/main")
  if [ "$pending" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "Auto-release: nothing new since $last_tag, skipping."
    exit 0
  fi
  # The 2h window runs from the RELEASE, not from the commit the tag points
  # at: commits can sit pending on main for hours before the cron/dispatch
  # cuts the tag (the common catch-up path), and reading the commit date
  # would let extra releases through exactly when this guard (and the
  # pub.dev ~12/day rate limit) exists to stop them (PR #1526 thread 5).
  # Annotated tags carry a tagger date; a lightweight tag (never cut by
  # this script, but defensive) falls back to the commit date.
  tag_ts=$(git for-each-ref --format='%(taggerdate:unix)' "refs/tags/$last_tag")
  [ -n "$tag_ts" ] || tag_ts=$(git log -1 --format=%ct "$last_tag")
  tag_age=$(( $(date +%s) - tag_ts ))
  if [ "$tag_age" -lt 7200 ]; then
    echo "Auto-release: coalesced — $last_tag is ${tag_age}s old (<2h); $pending commit(s) pending. Next eligible push or the 2h cron will release them."
    exit 0
  fi
fi

# Tag-push race honesty: a tag that appeared mid-run makes `next` stale —
# the push rejects it (already exists) and the retry loop re-derives from
# the freshly fetched tags. Never blind-push over an existing tag.
for attempt in 1 2 3; do
  git fetch origin main --tags --quiet

  latest_tag=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || true)
  if [ -z "$latest_tag" ]; then
    echo "::error::no vX.Y.Z tag found — refusing to invent a first version (cut v0.1.0 manually)." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  current="${latest_tag#v}"
  IFS='.' read -r major minor patch <<< "$current"
  next="$major.$minor.$((patch + 1))"
  tag="v$next"
  echo "Auto-release: $latest_tag -> $tag (attempt $attempt)"

  # The tag pins origin/main as of THIS fetch — a main that advances during
  # the run is picked up by a later release, never by a retag.
  git tag -a "$tag" -m "Release $tag" origin/main

  if [ "$dry_run" -eq 1 ]; then
    echo "Auto-release DRY-RUN: would push tag $tag at $(git rev-parse --short origin/main). No GitHub Release is created (gh-1801: the binaries job owns creation, draft-first)."
    git tag -d "$tag" >/dev/null
    exit 0
  fi

  if git push origin "refs/tags/$tag"; then
    echo "Auto-release: pushed $tag — the tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs fire from it."
    # gh-1801: NO release is created here. This script resolves an EMPTY
    # asset list — the CLI tarballs/SPA zip do not exist until the tag-run
    # binaries/web-spa jobs build them. Creating the release now would
    # publish an EMPTY `latest` immediately, and `fa update` would 404 on
    # fa-<os>-<arch>.tar.gz for every user until the binaries backfilled
    # (the v1.0.630 window, 2026-10-23: empty latest from 09:11 until
    # 09:14–09:20). A warning-only variant leaves the same window — the
    # skip is hard. The binaries job owns creation, draft-first, and
    # publishes only after its asset upload lands (pinned by
    # test/release_empty_latest_guard_test.dart).
    exit 0
  fi
  echo "Tag push raced (tag likely appeared mid-run), re-deriving..."
  git tag -d "$tag" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
done

echo "Auto-release failed after 3 attempts"
exit 1

# Note: n_1012_9c1a

Release-train recovery playbook (gh-1845, 2026-10-24): when a v* tag run's "Sign release checksums" (release-provenance) fails with "release <tag> is missing 1 required asset(s): fa-extension.zip — BLOCKING the publish", the fix is NOT code: dispatch the producer with an explicit tag — `gh workflow run build-macos.yml --ref <tag> -f version=<tag> -f create_release=true` (its build-extension job is ubuntu-latest, fast, and adopts the existing draft via scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh) — wait for fa-extension.zip to appear on the release, then `gh run rerun <tag-run-id> --failed`. Root pattern: build-macos.yml build-extension derives "latest+1 at its own dispatch moment" and runs ~once daily, so any tag train landing after the daily leg has no fa-extension.zip and the gh-1832 gate correctly strands it as a draft (seen stuck: v1.0.637, v1.0.638 on 2026-10-24). "Advance vpinned marker" failing right after is downstream noise (pin_release.sh refuses to pin unsigned releases) — it self-heals once provenance lands. Note: gh run view --json jobs returns only the latest attempt; failed release-tail jobs may be absent from a stale ci-red ticket's job list if the report was filed before the tail finished. Also: a rerun --failed never resurrects SKIPPED jobs (e.g. Installer smoke) — benign, the Quality gate treats skipped as neutral. Systemic fix (follow-up gh-1847) LANDED the same day: the tag train builds fa-extension.zip itself (ci.yml build-extension, an additive continue-on-error leg mirroring web-spa; release-provenance needs it so the gh-1832 gate never races the attach), so a draft stranded on the missing zip now self-heals with a plain `gh run rerun <tag-run-id> --failed` — the manual producer dispatch above survives only as the fallback for a red or flaky extension leg, and the daily build-macos leg was kept as the next-tag-draft pre-stager.

    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need

    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes

    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.

    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new

# gh-1899 — [daily-publish] stale release drafts swept

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The daily draft sweeper keeps finding stale bot drafts for freshly
released tags (v1.0.637, v1.0.639, v1.0.641) even though the release train
has per-job draft lifecycle guards — recurrence means a lifecycle guard is
missing (issue #282).

**Root cause**: Two distinct gaps, one per draft population:

1. **v1.0.641 — the duplicate-draft twin race (the recurring class).**
   `scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh` tolerates the view→create race with
   `|| true`, relying on GitHub to reject a second `gh release create` for
   the same tag. GitHub does **not** atomically enforce one release per
   tag: in run 40163369302 (v1.0.641, fully green), the `binaries-linux-arm64`
   leg and the `binaries-macos-arm64` leg both logged
   `✅ lazy draft ready for v1.0.641` 87 ms apart — **two draft release
   objects were created for the same tag** (precedent in the repo: duplicate
   published releases v0.1.120 ids 363745676/363745677, created the same
   second). The release-provenance job flips exactly ONE object to
   `--draft=false --latest`; the twin stays a draft forever. No failure-path
   guard can ever fire — every creating leg and the provenance job
   *succeeded* — so the only reclaimer is the 24h sweeper, which deletes the
   twin and files this recurring issue.

2. **v1.0.637 / v1.0.639 — drafts stranded by the gh-1832 required-assets
   gate.** The tag runs 40103891305 / 40131265943 failed at "Assert required
   release assets (gh-1832 gate)" with `missing 1 required asset(s):
   fa-extension.zip`. Stranding the draft is intentional (recovery window
   for `gh run rerun --failed`, memory n_1012), and the missing producer was
   fixed systemically by gh-1847 (the tag train builds fa-extension.zip
   itself since 2026-10-25). These two drafts predate that fix.

**Impact**: Every tag train with a concurrent lazy-draft create can leave an
orphan twin draft; the sweeper then deletes it after 24h and files a
deduplicated sweep issue (gh-1899). Sweep-time deletion also permanently
removes a gate-stranded tag's only release when nobody recovers within 24h
(v1.0.637/v1.0.639 have no release page at all now).

**Fix approach**: Add the missing post-publish lifecycle guard — a
run-scoped draft **dedupe** step that runs after the provenance
`--draft=false --latest` flip (and after the attach path's servable-recovery
flip): the tag's release is published and servable at that point, so any
DRAFT left for the same tag carrying THIS run's ownership marker
(`release-draft-owner: run/<id>/job/<name>`) is a proven orphan twin whose
assets are unpublished-only (issue #282 E2) — delete it. Foreign/unmarked
drafts keep the existing ownership discipline (left for the 24h sweeper),
mirroring `scripts/release_draft_guard.sh`. Wired as
`scripts/release_draft_dedupe.sh` called from ci.yml release-provenance
(after the flip) and `scripts/release_attach_or_create.sh` `upload_all`
(after the servable-recovery flip). With twins reclaimed at publish time,
sweeps come up clean and the self-closing issue lifecycle closes gh-1899.

**Previous attempt**: none — first development pass on gh-1899.

# crap4dart loc-scope companion configuration for flutter_agent_harness.
# https://github.com/IstiN/crap4dart
#
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS (issue #1234 rework): crap4dart 0.11.0 has no
# per-gate `sources` override — `gates.loc.sources` is rejected as an
# unknown key (ConfigException; caught by CI on 019ede65). The package
# config's top-level `sources` drives the CRAP census too, so it must
# stay [lib, bin]. This companion config runs the SAME loc gate over the
# one slice the package config cannot express: test/ + example/ — the
# exact scope the retired shell guards (gh-1232 stage_size + the ci.yml
# find-exec jobs) scanned there. flutter_app/lib stays under
# flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.
#
# RATCHET: max_lines mirrors both package configs (2800, wc -l
# semantics, generated output excluded); max_lines only DOWN.
# Enforcement: whole-tree in CI (guards job, `check --config` step) and
# staged files in scripts/pre-commit — the same two points as the
# package configs.

sources: [test, example]

exclude:
  - '**.g.dart'
  - '**.freezed.dart'
  - '**.mocks.dart'
  - 'build/**'
  - 'vendor/**'

# CRAP analysis is the package config's job (threshold pinned there);
# this config is loc-only, so no coverage input is read.
crap:
  enabled: false

coverage:
  required: false
  run_tests: false
  branch_coverage: false

# 0.9.5 default-enables ALL built-in gates; only loc is enforced here,
# everything else disabled explicitly so a bare `check` means exactly
# the ≤2800-line ceiling over test/ + example/.
gates:
  loc:
    enabled: true
    max_lines: 2800
    exclude:
      - '**.g.dart'
      - '**.freezed.dart'
      - '**.mocks.dart'
  test_coverage: {enabled: false}
  complexity: {enabled: false}
  method_size: {enabled: false}
  nesting: {enabled: false}
  class_size: {enabled: false}
  weight_of_class: {enabled: false}
  unused_code: {enabled: false}
  unused_files: {enabled: false}
  banned_imports: {enabled: false}
  duplication: {enabled: false}
  file_naming: {enabled: false}
  magic_constants: {enabled: false}
  test_assertions: {enabled: false}
  folder_structure: {enabled: false}
  external: {enabled: false}
  public_docs: {enabled: false}
  golden: {enabled: false} # flutter-only gate (core is not a Flutter project)
  accessibility: {enabled: false}
  hardcoded_strings: {enabled: false}
  broken_goldens: {enabled: false}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Post-publish orphan-draft twin cleanup (gh-1899).
#
# Why this exists: GitHub does NOT atomically enforce one release per tag.
# The lazy draft create (scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh) tolerates the
# view→create race with `|| true` on the assumption that a second
# `gh release create` for the same tag is rejected — it is not always:
# run 40163369302 (v1.0.641, fully green) created TWO draft releases for
# the same tag 87 ms apart (both binaries legs logged "lazy draft ready";
# duplicate-tag precedent: v0.1.120, release ids 363745676/363745677).
# release-provenance flips exactly ONE object to --draft=false --latest;
# the twin stays a draft forever — no failure-path guard can fire because
# every creating leg SUCCEEDED — so the only reclaimer was the 24h
# sweeper, which deleted the twin and filed the recurring
# "[daily-publish] stale release drafts swept" issue (gh-1899).
#
# This is the missing success-path half of the issue #282 invariant ("a
# run ends with its draft published or deleted — never orphaned") — the
# failure half lives in scripts/release_draft_guard.sh. Call it AFTER the
# publish flip (ci.yml release-provenance's "Upload provenance assets",
# release_attach_or_create.sh's servable-recovery publish):
#
#   - PRECONDITION: the tag must have a PUBLISHED release. A red
#     provenance (gh-1832 gate, signing) leaves the draft on purpose — it
#     is the recovery vessel for `gh run rerun --failed` — and this guard
#     must never take it away. No published release → no-op.
#   - Deletes every DRAFT for <tag> stamped with THIS run's ownership
#     marker (<!-- release-draft-owner: run/<GITHUB_RUN_ID>/job/<name> -->)
#     by release id via the API — those are proven orphan twins of the
#     just-published release, carrying unpublished-only assets (issue
#     #282 E2). The tag-based `gh release delete` is never used: under
#     duplicate releases a tag lookup is ambiguous, the very class this
#     guard exists for.
#   - Foreign-run and unmarked drafts are NEVER deleted here — the same
#     ownership discipline as release_draft_guard.sh; the daily sweeper
#     (scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh) reclaims those after 24h.
#
# Usage: release_draft_dedupe.sh <tag>
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GITHUB_RUN_ID (Actions defaults), GH_TOKEN/
#      GITHUB_TOKEN.
set -euo pipefail

tag="${1:?usage: release_draft_dedupe.sh <tag>}"
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
: "${GITHUB_RUN_ID:?GITHUB_RUN_ID must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}"

# One listing, two questions. `gh api --paginate` concatenates one JSON
# array per page; -s flattens them into a single release roster before
# the filter runs (a per-page filter could miss a twin on another page).
list=$(gh api --paginate "repos/$repo/releases")

# PRECONDITION: the tag's release is published. Until the flip happens,
# a leftover draft is the recovery vessel, not an orphan.
if ! printf '%s' "$list" | jq -s -e --arg tag "$tag" \
    'flatten | any(.[]; .tag_name == $tag and .draft == false)' \
    >/dev/null; then
  echo "release draft dedupe: no published release for $tag — a leftover draft is the rerun --failed recovery vessel; nothing reclaimed (gh-1899)"
  exit 0
fi

# The marker's run segment is matched with its trailing slash so run/111
# can never match run/1111 (the prefix trap release_draft_guard.sh pins).
twins=$(printf '%s' "$list" | jq -s -r --arg tag "$tag" --arg run "run/$GITHUB_RUN_ID/" '
  [ flatten
    | .[]
    | select(.draft == true and .tag_name == $tag
        and ((.body // "") | contains("release-draft-owner: " + $run)))
    | .id | tostring ]
  | join("\n")')

if [ -z "$twins" ]; then
  echo "release draft dedupe: nothing to reclaim for $tag (no own-run twin drafts)"
  exit 0
fi

deleted=0
while IFS= read -r id; do
  [ -n "$id" ] || continue
  gh api -X DELETE "repos/$repo/releases/$id" >/dev/null
  deleted=$((deleted + 1))
  echo "::warning::release draft dedupe: deleted orphaned twin draft $id for $tag — the lazy-create race minted two releases for one tag and only one could be published (gh-1899); its assets were unpublished-only, the published release is the artifact store (issue #282 E2)"
done <<< "$twins"

echo "release draft dedupe: reclaimed $deleted orphaned twin draft(s) for $tag (gh-1899)"

arguments.content:
### Root Cause

- GitHub does not atomically enforce one release per tag: two legs racing the lazy draft create can BOTH succeed. In run 40163369302 (v1.0.641, fully green) `binaries-linux-arm64` and `binaries-macos-arm64` both logged "lazy draft ready" 87 ms apart — twin drafts. release-provenance flips exactly one to published; the twin rots until the 24h sweeper deletes it and files this recurring issue. No failure-path guard can fire — every creating leg succeeded.
- v1.0.637/v1.0.639 were the older gh-1832 class (missing `fa-extension.zip` stranded the draft on the required-assets gate); the systemic producer fix (gh-1847, tag train builds the zip itself) already landed 2026-10-25.

### Fix

- `scripts/release_draft_dedupe.sh` (new): post-publish guard — after the `--draft=false --latest` flip, deletes leftover DRAFTs for the tag stamped with THIS run's `release-draft-owner` marker (proven orphan twins; unpublished-only assets, issue #282 E2). Precondition: the tag must have a published release — a red provenance keeps the draft as the `rerun --failed` recovery vessel. Foreign/unmarked drafts are never touched (same ownership discipline as `release_draft_guard.sh`; the 24h sweeper reclaims those). Deletes by release id via the API — a tag-based delete is ambiguous under duplicate releases, the very class this guard exists for.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` release-provenance: new success-path step "Reclaim orphaned draft twins (gh-1899)" right after the publish flip.
- `scripts/release_attach_or_create.sh`: `upload_all` runs the same dedupe after its servable-recovery flip (daily legs share the race-prone lazy create).
- With twins reclaimed at publish time, sweeps come up clean and the self-closing issue lifecycle auto-closes gh-1899.

### Test Coverage

- `test/release_draft_dedupe_test.dart` (new, 9 tests, RED-first): two own-run twins deleted by id with everything else untouched; foreign-run + unmarked drafts never deleted; no-published-release → no-op (recovery window); clean no-op; run-id prefix trap (`run/1111` ≠ `run/111`); multi-page listing; wiring lints (dedupe step ordered AFTER the flip in ci.yml and release_attach_or_create.sh). All 9 PASSED (also re-run in a clean-env fresh subprocess).
- Regression: `test/release_hygiene_test.dart` 52/52 PASSED; release suite (attach-or-create mint, flow race, empty-latest guard, gh-1847 train, required-assets gate, dedupe guard) 113/113 PASSED; full non-integration suite result below.

### Notes

- v1.0.637/v1.0.639 tags currently have no release page (drafts swept before recovery); the recovery playbook for future gh-1832 strands is unchanged — the dedupe never touches a draft while its tag is unpublished.
- The sweeper itself is untouched: it stays the 24h backstop for foreign/unmarked orphans.

content.text:
### Root Cause

- GitHub does not atomically enforce one release per tag: two legs racing the lazy draft create can BOTH succeed. In run 40163369302 (v1.0.641, fully green) `binaries-linux-arm64` and `binaries-macos-arm64` both logged "lazy draft ready" 87 ms apart — twin drafts. release-provenance flips exactly one to published; the twin rots until the 24h sweeper deletes it and files this recurring issue. No failure-path guard can fire — every creating leg succeeded.
- v1.0.637/v1.0.639 were the older gh-1832 class (missing `fa-extension.zip` stranded the draft on the required-assets gate); the systemic producer fix (gh-1847, tag train builds the zip itself) already landed 2026-10-25.

### Fix

- `scripts/release_draft_dedupe.sh` (new): post-publish guard — after the `--draft=false --latest` flip, deletes leftover DRAFTs for the tag stamped with THIS run's `release-draft-owner` marker (proven orphan twins; unpublished-only assets, issue #282 E2). Precondition: the tag must have a published release — a red provenance keeps the draft as the `rerun --failed` recovery vessel. Foreign/unmarked drafts are never touched (same ownership discipline as `release_draft_guard.sh`; the 24h sweeper reclaims those). Deletes by release id via the API — a tag-based delete is ambiguous under duplicate releases, the very class this guard exists for.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` release-provenance: new success-path step "Reclaim orphaned draft twins (gh-1899)" right after the publish flip.
- `scripts/release_attach_or_create.sh`: `upload_all` runs the same dedupe after its servable-recovery flip (daily legs share the race-prone lazy create).
- With twins reclaimed at publish time, sweeps come up clean and the self-closing issue lifecycle auto-closes gh-1899.

### Test Coverage

- `test/release_draft_dedupe_test.dart` (new, 9 tests, RED-first): two own-run twins deleted by id with everything else untouched; foreign-run + unmarked drafts never deleted; no-published-release → no-op (recovery window); clean no-op; run-id prefix trap (`run/1111` ≠ `run/111`); multi-page listing; wiring lints (dedupe step ordered AFTER the flip in ci.yml and release_attach_or_create.sh). All 9 PASSED (also re-run in a clean-env fresh subprocess).
- Regression: `test/release_hygiene_test.dart` 52/52 PASSED; release suite (attach-or-create mint, flow race, empty-latest guard, gh-1847 train, required-assets gate, dedupe guard) 113/113 PASSED; full non-integration suite result below.

### Notes

- v1.0.637/v1.0.639 tags currently have no release page (drafts swept before recovery); the recovery playbook for future gh-1832 strands is unchanged — the dedupe never touches a draft while its tag is unpublished.
- The sweeper itself is untouched: it stays the 24h backstop for foreign/unmarked orphans.

Wired into ci.yml `release-provenance` (after the flip) and `release_attach_or_create.sh` `upload_all` (after the servable-recovery flip). Deletes by release id — tag-based deletes are ambiguous under duplicate releases.
